q-5658.name: Question 1
q-5658.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14200665/assets/2e054a16d93658d53cc9dc16e3fe5544b9a007721d1d9c2f87581799a6257797.png)

What is the diameter of a circle that has an area of $36\pi ?$
q-5658.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of a circle is $A=\pi {r}^{2}$, where $r$ is the radius. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ 36\pi  & =\pi {r}^{2} \\ 36\cancel{\pi } & =\cancel{\pi }{r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =36 \\ r & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the diameter is

$$
d=2\cdot r=2\cdot 6=12.
$$

A=πr236π=πr236π=πr2r2=36r=6.

q-79024.name: Question 3
q-79024.problem: What is the area of a circle that has a diameter of $4?$
q-79024.worked_solution:
The radius of a circle is half the diameter. So, the radius of our circle is $r=2.$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
